brief: #145 put the town in the water with five casters — bridge, deck, mill wheel, jetty, willow. Two things have landed on the river since and drawWaterMirror knows about neither. (a) #155's reeds: a 56-cell fringe footed along the bank, carrying an in-line image but absent from riverCasters(), whose per-caster clip+gradient+chop pass assumes ONE thing at ONE row and will need to handle a run. (b) #151's terrace shadow now falls on the NEAR river, 19 down to 1 sub-cells over rows 79-87, which is water-only there — so the town's own shade sits on top of the mirror instead of darkening it. Both are the same seam. Do them together.
successLooksLike: A reed run stands in the water beneath itself, and on a low sun the terrace's shadow on the near river reads as shade IN the water rather than a quad floating over it. Same-code pixel control 0; the feature's mass quoted as a ratio to that floor, day and evening.
avoid: Leave the BOATS out — c233 names them as the class #145 omitted and they are a brief of their own, not a rider on this one. The mirror is the shadow solve with the eye for the sun, a NEGATIVE z, so a caster's own draw IS its image and every draw landing on the plane must read the sign. Watch that nothing double-darkens where the shadow and the image overlap.
